name: 터미널
description: 터미널 프로그램을 실행하는 터미널 카드. 커서, 글꼴, 셸, 스크롤바를 설정한다.
icon: <rect x="2" y="3" width="12" height="10" rx="2"/><circle cx="5" cy="7" r="1.5"/><path d="M8 9l2-2m-2 0l2 2"/>

cursor.shape.label: 커서 모양
cursor.shape.description: block은 칸 전체, underline은 밑줄, beam은 세로 막대로 그린다. 프로그램이 모양을 정하면 그 모양을 쓴다.

cursor.blink.label: 커서 깜박임
cursor.blink.description: Never는 늘 멈추고 Always는 늘 깜박인다. Off는 멈춘 채로 시작하고 On은 깜박이며 시작하며, 둘 다 프로그램의 요청을 따른다.

cursor.idleTimeout.label: 깜박임 멈춤 시간(ms)
cursor.idleTimeout.description: 입력이 없으면 이 시간 뒤 깜박임을 멈춘다. 0이면 멈추지 않는다.

cursor.unfocused.label: 포커스 밖 커서
cursor.unfocused.description: 터미널이 입력을 받지 않을 때의 커서. hollow는 빈 네모, solid는 채운 네모, underline과 beam은 그 모양이며, unchanged는 포커스가 있을 때와 같다.

clipboard.program.label: 프로그램의 클립보드 사용
clipboard.program.description: 터미널 프로그램이 OSC 52 요청으로 클립보드를 쓰고 읽는 것을 정한다. write는 쓰기만 허용하고 읽기는 막으며, allow는 둘 다 허용하고, deny는 둘 다 막는다. 막힌 요청은 오류로 보이지 않고 기록된다. 사용자가 직접 복사하고 붙여넣는 것에는 영향이 없다.

font.family.label: 글꼴
font.family.description: 세미콜론으로 나눈 글꼴 이름. 앞의 글꼴부터 쓴다.

shell.label: 셸
shell.description: login은 계정의 로그인 셸이다. 다른 값은 실행 파일의 절대 경로다.

title.label: 탭 제목
title.description: program은 프로그램이 보낸 제목을 탭에 보이고, name은 프로그램 제목을 쓰지 않고 탭 이름을 유지한다.

notifications.label: 알림 전달
notifications.description: tab은 탭에만 알리고, system은 운영체제 알림 센터를 사용한다. 호스트가 system을 지원하지 않으면 오류를 보인다.

scrollbar.track.label: 스크롤바 바탕
scrollbar.track.description: terminal은 터미널 바탕색이다. 다른 값은 #rrggbb 또는 #rrggbbaa 색이다.

scrollReadQuiet.label: 스크롤 읽기 조용한 간격(frame)
scrollReadQuiet.description: terminal.screen.scroll.read 가 프로그램의 출력 없이 이만큼의 display frame 이 지나면 그 단계의 그리기가 끝났다고 본다. 동기 update 로 그리는 프로그램은 그 끝에서 곧바로 끝난다.

scrollbar.shape.label: 스크롤바 모양
scrollbar.shape.description: rounded는 둥근 끝, square는 각진 끝.

padding.top.label: 위쪽 여백(pt)
padding.top.description: 터미널 격자와 표면 가장자리 사이의 간격. 여백은 터미널 바탕색이다.

padding.right.label: 오른쪽 여백(pt)
padding.right.description: 터미널 격자와 표면 가장자리 사이의 간격. 여백은 터미널 바탕색이다.

padding.bottom.label: 아래쪽 여백(pt)
padding.bottom.description: 터미널 격자와 표면 가장자리 사이의 간격. 여백은 터미널 바탕색이다.

padding.left.label: 왼쪽 여백(pt)
padding.left.description: 터미널 격자와 표면 가장자리 사이의 간격. 여백은 터미널 바탕색이다.

status.name: terminal.screen
status.description: The latest terminal screen cell rows, updated on sidecar screen events.

status.name: terminal.session
status.description: The session state: identifier, dimensions, cell size, the scrollback viewport offset, the history rows of the active screen and the rows dropped from the primary history as `scrollback {offset, history, dropped}`, whether the alternate screen is active with the rows kept above it and the kept rows dropped as `alternate {active, history, dropped}`, the foreground program of the terminal as `foreground {group, pid, command, arguments, cwd, started}` and its background jobs as `background`, each a job of the same form with `state` (`running` or `stopped`), which the sidecar reads after each output and at each exit and signal of a job (`command`, `arguments`, `cwd` and `started` null with `error` when the system refused a read of the process; `foreground` null when the foreground group has no process; both null while the list is not known, before the first read and after a failed read, which the session shows), which terminal.process.list reads at the time of a call, the number of selection releases the sidecar answered, the pointer shape the program set with OSC 22, the theme mode and the default background (`#rrggbb`) the sidecar applied, the reasons of the last eight output sequences the engine rejected, and the input held by the sidecar as `inputHeld`, which is `{queued, held}` while held and `null` otherwise, and whether the child of the session ended as `exited`.

status.name: terminal.cursor
status.description: The terminal cursor position and the rendering policy, shape, blink request and preedit drawn by the sidecar, together with the frame-effective nullable caret and required nullable render metadata from the same screen event; null means no matching draw.

status.name: terminal.activity
status.description: The core activity level of the terminal, derived from terminal.program and terminal.state (core docs/spec/terminal-state.md#activity): the highest level of the program status records (`attention` for blocked, `failed` for error, `running` for working, `idle` for idle and done); else `attention` for a notice; else `idle` for idle, `running` for running, `failed` for an exited command with a nonzero exit code and for the idle state after it until the next command runs, and null for no activity, before the first mark and for an exited command with exit 0 or no exit code. It notifies only when the level changes.

status.name: terminal.program
status.description: The program status of the session (core docs/spec/terminal-state.md#plugin-program-status): `records` are the OSC 7501 records of the program in the terminal, the root record first and then by id, each {id, state, kind, progress, app, title, msg} with state idle, working, blocked, done or error; `notice` is whether the program called the person by a notification or a bell while the terminal had no keyboard focus, which ends when the person focuses or types into the terminal and at the end of the command; `sequence` is the number of the last change from 1 (0 before the first). A blocked record states that the program waits for an approval or an answer; a running command without records is a program whose wait is unknown. The page reads it after the session opens or attaches and follows each change event of the sidecar.

status.name: terminal.messages
status.description: The messages folder that the terminal registered with its sidecar (core docs/spec/messaging.md#folder-of-a-terminal): folder is <root>/.soksak/messages/<surface> of the project of the window, which the sidecar creates, and registration is the identifier of the registration, the epoch of the cursor of terminal.messages.read and terminal.messages.wait. It is null before the reply, in a window without a project, while the sidecar connection is down and after the registration closes. A refused or closed registration is shown as the error terminal.messages: <error>: <reason>. held is null while nothing holds the injection of the messages and {reason, kind, pending} while a hold applies (core docs/spec/messaging.md#hold-for-the-person), and last is null before the first decision and then {seq, path, from, state, reason} of the last message that the page injected, refused or skipped (core docs/spec/messaging.md#delivery).

status.name: terminal.state
status.description: The terminal state of the session from the OSC 133 marks of its shell: `state` is `idle`, `running`, `exited` or null before the first mark, `source` is `osc133` or null, `sequence` is the number of the last change from 1 (0 before the first), and `exit` is the exit code of `exited`, from 0 to 255, or null. The page reads it after the session opens or attaches and follows each change event of the sidecar.

commands.name: terminal.input
commands.description: Sends the bytes to the terminal session as one input as UTF-8 text and does not add Enter; a program that submits a line must use terminal.submit.

commands.name: terminal.submit
commands.description: terminal.submit sends its text as one paste, which the sidecar brackets when the program enabled bracketed paste mode, and Enter as a separate input after the reply of the paste, refuses text that contains CR or LF, and returns only that the sidecar answered both inputs; confirm acceptance from the status of the input line and of the agent busy state, never by waiting with a timer.

commands.name: terminal.focus
commands.description: Transfers keyboard ownership to the terminal native image region.

commands.name: terminal.screen.read
commands.description: Requests the screen that the terminal shows now and returns its cell rows and the frame that shows them; each cell has ch and width, and a cell of width 0 continues a wide character. The rows follow the viewport: after terminal.scrollback.set they are the rows at that offset, and while a full-screen program shows the alternate screen they are the rows that the program drew. Read mode Visible: use it for the rows on the screen now; it cannot see the rows above the viewport, which terminal.screen.rows reads without input to the program; check terminal.session first: alternate.active tells whether a full-screen program holds the screen and foreground names the program.

commands.name: terminal.screen.rows
commands.description: Returns count rows (1 to 200) from row from of the rows that the terminal keeps for screen, with their cell rows and the plain text of each row, without moving the viewport. Read mode Kept rows: screen is primary or alternate, screen is required, and no input reaches the program. screen primary reads the primary screen and its history: the history of a shell and of a program that draws inline, where row 0 is the first row that entered the history, the oldest kept row is scrollback.dropped of terminal.session, and the viewport at offset 0 starts scrollback.history rows after it. screen alternate reads the rows that a full-screen program scrolled off the alternate screen followed by the rows of that screen, where row 0 is the first row kept since the program entered the alternate screen and the oldest kept row is alternate.dropped; use it while alternate.active is true and after the program left, until it enters the alternate screen again. A range outside the kept rows is refused with the kept range. It cannot see the rows that the program never drew, which terminal.screen.scroll.read reads.

commands.name: terminal.messages.read
commands.description: Returns the messages of the registered folder of the terminal whose seq is above after (core docs/spec/messaging.md#mcp-tools). after is an integer of at least 0 and defaults to 0; registration is the registration of terminal.messages and is required when after is above 0; the command takes no other member. The reply is {registration, messages: [{seq, path, text, from}], last}: pass last as the next after with that registration. A registration that is not current fails with epoch-changed, and the read starts again from after 0 with the current registration; a terminal without a registered folder fails with unknown-terminal.

commands.name: terminal.messages.wait
commands.description: Waits until the registered folder of the terminal holds a message whose seq is above after and returns the messages as terminal.messages.read does (core docs/spec/messaging.md#mcp-tools); it has no time limit and ends on arrival, with registration-closed when the registration closes, or when the sidecar connection ends. after is an integer of at least 0 and defaults to 0; registration is the registration of terminal.messages and is required when after is above 0; the command takes no other member. The reply is {registration, messages: [{seq, path, text, from}], last}: pass last as the next after with that registration. A registration that is not current fails with epoch-changed, and the read starts again from after 0 with the current registration; a terminal without a registered folder fails with unknown-terminal.

commands.name: terminal.screen.scroll.read
commands.description: Scrolls the program by by lines (positive toward older content), reads the screen after the program has drawn it, scrolls back by -by and reads the screen again. Read mode Program scroll: use it only for text that the program never drew, which terminal.screen.read and terminal.screen.rows cannot see; input reaches the program, by the wheel route of the terminal without Shift: a mouse report when the program enabled mouse tracking, the cursor keys of the alternate scroll on the alternate screen, and the viewport of the primary screen otherwise. by is required, an integer from -1000 to 1000 other than 0, relative to the position of the program when the read starts. The result holds route (program, alternate_scroll or viewport), changed (false when the screen after the scroll equals the first read, the end of the content), text (the plain text of each row after the scroll), restored (whether the last read equals the first read), settledBy {scroll, restore} (sync, quiet or viewport, the event that ended the wait of each step), quiet (the setting scrollReadQuiet in display frames) and refreshRate (null when the read received no display frame); when restored is false it also holds first {before, after}, the first row of the first and of the last read, and the session shows the error, because the program is not where it was. Input of the person during the read ends it with the error scrollReadInterrupted, and the input runs.

commands.name: terminal.process.list
commands.description: Reads the process list of the terminal at the time of the call: the foreground program, the process of the foreground process group that holds the terminal (the shell while it waits at its prompt), and the background jobs, one for each other process group of the terminal except the group of the shell, in ascending order of the group. Each has group (the process group, which identifies a job while its processes end), pid, command (the path of its executable), arguments (the arguments after the program name, which identify an agent with its session file), cwd and started (milliseconds since the Unix epoch); a job also has state, running or stopped. When the system refused a read of a process, command, arguments, cwd and started are null and error names the read. foreground is null when the foreground group has no process. terminal.session holds the same list as the sidecar last sent it.

commands.name: terminal.image.inline.delete
commands.description: Deletes one named inline image owned by this terminal session.

commands.name: terminal.cursor.set
commands.description: Sets the terminal cursor rendering policy.

commands.name: terminal.scrollback.set
commands.description: Moves the terminal viewport to offset lines above the newest output (0 is the newest), limited to the retained history, without writing to the program; terminal.screen.read then returns the rows at that offset. The alternate screen of a full-screen program keeps no history, so the command does not scroll such a program.

commands.name: terminal.link.open
commands.description: Opens a URI from a terminal hyperlink with the user's default application through the host; the host accepts http, https, and mailto.

commands.name: terminal.copy
commands.description: Copies the text of the current terminal selection to the clipboard; without a selection the clipboard is unchanged.

commands.name: terminal.paste
commands.description: Reads one user-selected text, file, or PNG clipboard payload and pastes it once without executing it.

commands.name: terminal.drop
commands.description: Pastes user-dropped local file URLs once without executing them.

element.name: terminal.scrollbar
element.description: The scrollbar track shown while the terminal retains history; at the newest output its thumb is at the bottom of the track.

element.name: terminal.scrollbar.thumb
element.description: The scrollbar thumb; dragging it moves the viewport.
